Chapter 6 Taxonomic shares of Hill power sums

The diversity and pairwise beta diversity chapters describe whole communities. Here we use hilldiv3::hillshare() to allocate each sample’s Hill power sum to sets of representative MAGs. A share is a fraction between zero and one, not a fraction of the effective Hill number reported by hilldiv(). The calculation is descriptive; it does not test whether a phylum is enriched in a habitat.

This chapter was rendered with hilldiv3 version 3.1.0.

6.1 Define the genome sets

We use four phyla with contrasting profiles across the panel. The Other set contains every remaining representative, so the five sets are disjoint and exhaustive. Each representative stands for its published 95% ANI cluster; the shares describe those cluster profiles, not the abundance of every MAG within a cluster.

phylum <- sub("^p__", "", genome_metadata$phylum)
focus_phyla <- c("Pseudomonadota", "Actinomycetota",
                  "Acidobacteriota", "Bacteroidota")
share_sets <- lapply(focus_phyla, function(name) {
  genome_metadata$genome_id[phylum == name]
})
names(share_sets) <- focus_phyla
share_sets$Other <- genome_metadata$genome_id[!phylum %in% focus_phyla]
stopifnot(sum(lengths(share_sets)) == nrow(genome_metadata),
          setequal(unlist(share_sets, use.names = FALSE),
                   genome_metadata$genome_id))

hillshare() returns one row for each sample, order, diversity type, and set. The phylogenetic call uses the same representative tree as the earlier chapters. Both diversity types are requested together.

shares <- hilldiv3::hillshare(
  overview_abundance, q = c(0, 1, 2), tree = genome_tree,
  type = c("neutral", "phylogenetic"), sets = share_sets
)

6.2 Shares across habitats

The heatmap shows the median share among the 45 samples in each habitat. Its colour scale is the same in every panel. At neutral \(q=1\), a set’s share equals its summed relative abundance. At \(q=0\), each detected representative has equal neutral weight; at \(q=2\), abundant representatives carry more weight. Phylogenetic shares also allocate the weights of tree branches to their descendant representatives.

ggplot2::ggplot(share_medians,
                ggplot2::aes(x = Habitat, y = Set, fill = share)) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "#f7f7f7", high = "#8b1e1e", limits = c(0, 1),
    labels = function(x) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * x), name = "Median share"
  ) +
  ggplot2::facet_grid(Order ~ Type) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1),
    strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold")
  )

Median power-sum shares in each habitat. Medians are taken separately for each set, so the displayed medians need not sum to one; the five shares sum to one within every individual sample, type, and order.

The selected phyla show different habitat patterns. Bacteroidota contributes little neutral \(q=1\) weight in most soil samples but substantially more in saltwater sediment and wastewater. The next figure retains the sample-level values behind that contrast.

ggplot2::ggplot(bacteroidota,
                ggplot2::aes(x = share, y = habitat)) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.55,
                        fill = "#e6c7c7", colour = "#702626") +
  ggplot2::geom_jitter(height = 0.13, width = 0, alpha = 0.4,
                       size = 0.8, colour = "#702626") +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
    labels = function(x) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * x),
    expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.03))
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Bacteroidota share, neutral q = 1", y = NULL) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank())

Each point is one sample; boxes show medians and interquartile ranges. A zero means no representative from this phylum was detected in that sample.

The median Bacteroidota share is 24.9% in wastewater and 11.1% in saltwater sediment. It is zero in agricultural field soil, where the phylum is detected in only 3 of 45 selected samples.

6.3 How order and tree weighting change a share

For Pseudomonadota, the next plot compares sample medians and interquartile ranges across orders in four habitats. The lines connect summaries, not individual samples. A shared vertical scale makes both diversity types directly visible.

ggplot2::ggplot(share_order,
                ggplot2::aes(x = q, y = median, colour = Type, group = Type)) +
  ggplot2::geom_errorbar(ggplot2::aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
                         width = 0.09, linewidth = 0.5) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 1, 2)) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.2),
    labels = function(x) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * x)
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = c("Neutral" = "#702626",
                                          "Phylogenetic" = "#1b6b75")) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ habitat, ncol = 2) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Diversity order (q)", y = "Pseudomonadota share",
                colour = NULL) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
                 strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"))

Points are medians across 45 samples; bars are interquartile ranges. They describe the selected panel and are not confidence intervals.

The phylogenetic tree is rooted but not ultrametric. At \(q=1\), differences between neutral and phylogenetic shares reflect root-to-tip path lengths in addition to abundance. At other orders, shared branch weights also affect the allocation. The panel has no matched functional-distance matrix, so we restrict this example to neutral and phylogenetic shares. Habitat and sampling year are partly confounded; these figures do not establish a habitat effect.
